# Welcome Scope

## How To Build

A WelcomeScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A WelcomeScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

A welcome page that checks what Suspense needs is installed and working, says plainly what isn't, and guides each fix, so Suspense is ready before the first prompt is sent rather than failing on it.

### Shape

#### Description

Shown in an [InsetPanelScope](../../ui/components/inset-panel/index.md#inset-panel-scope), as the settings are, headed "Welcome to Suspense", with a close button whose tooltip says it closes the welcome page. Beneath the heading, a muted line says that Suspense runs coding harnesses on a project's code and spec, and checks here that what it needs is in place. Then a checklist, one row per check, in order, and at its foot a "Check again" button, and a line saying whether Suspense is ready.

#### Checks

Each check is a row: a status icon, a green check when it passes, a red cross when a required check fails, an amber warning when an optional one does, and a spinner while it is being checked; the check's name; muted beside it what was found, as the version a command reports; and, beneath, while it fails, a line of guidance saying what is wrong, why Suspense needs it, and how to fix it, with the action that fixes it where Suspense can take one. The checks go in this order.

- "Git", found by running `git --version`, required, since projects are git repositories. Missing, its guidance links to https://git-scm.com/downloads.
- "Piton", found by running `piton --version`, required, since the spec is built, sliced, and checked with it. Missing, its guidance links to https://github.com/piton-lang/piton-rs.
- "Harness", the harness in use, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, found by running its command with `--version`, required, since Code tasks run it on the host. Missing, its guidance names the command and links to the harness's installation instructions, https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/setup for Claude Code, https://github.com/openai/codex for Codex, and https://opencode.ai/docs/ for OpenCode, with a "Choose another harness" button that opens the Agent section of the [SettingsWindowScope](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope).
- "Podman", found by running `podman --version`, required, since Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps, and questions run in a container, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says. Missing, its guidance links to Podman's installation instructions for the platform, as it gives them.
- "Podman machine", on macOS and Windows only, required, passing while a Podman machine is running. With none, its guidance offers "Set up Podman", and with one stopped, "Start Podman", each as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says, what the command prints shown beneath the row as it runs. It is checked only once Podman is found, and shows "Needs Podman", muted, until then.
- "Containers", required, passing once Podman runs a container for the application, as by running `podman info`. Failing, its guidance says Podman couldn't be accessed, with what Podman printed, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says. It is checked only once the checks above it pass.
- "Harness login", required, passing while the harness in use is logged in in its container, read from its volume. Not logged in, its guidance offers "Log in", which shows the login view, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says. It is checked only once "Containers" passes.

Every check runs in the background, all at once where they don't wait on one another, as each command is run without a console window, never holding up the window. A command that takes longer than 10 seconds fails its check, saying it didn't answer.

#### Ready

Suspense is ready when every required check passes, and the line at the checklist's foot then reads "Suspense is ready", with a "Get started" button that closes the welcome page; otherwise it reads how many checks still need attention, as "2 things need attention", and Get started is not shown, the close button closing the page all the same, since what passes still works.
"Check again" runs every check anew. A check whose action, as setting up Podman or logging in, finishes runs again by itself, and so do the checks waiting on it. A link opened in the browser leaves the page as it is, until Check again.

#### Opening

At each launch, Suspense runs the checks in the background as it starts. If any required check fails, the welcome page opens over the main window once they are done, unless the user has turned off "Show at launch when something needs attention", a checkbox at the page's foot, on until turned off, remembered for the user. When every check passes, nothing is shown.
It can be opened at any time with the Welcome command, a "Welcome" button with a checklist icon in a "Help" group, the last group of the [RibbonApplicationTabScope](../../ui/components/ribbon/application-tab/index.md#ribbon-application-tab-scope), after Preferences, whose tooltip says it checks that Suspense is ready to run. It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon leaves it out. Opening it runs every check anew. It needs no project, and works the same with or without one.

The Welcome page is built: it checks what Suspense needs, opens at launch when something fails, and can be reopened from Application → Help → Welcome. All 494 tests pass, but I haven't opened it in the running app or run the real checks on this machine.

**The page:** it opens in the same floating panel as Settings, headed "Welcome to Suspense", with a close button. There's a short intro line, then one row per check in the spec's order.
- **Row status:** a spinner while running, a green check when it passes, a red cross when it fails. A check waiting on another shows "Needs Podman", "Needs Containers" or "Needs the checks above".
- **What was found:** the version shows beside the check's name, read from `--version`.
- **When a check fails:** it says what's wrong, why Suspense needs it, and how to fix it, with these fix buttons:

| Check | Fix offered |
|---|---|
| Git | Download Git |
| Piton | Install Piton |
| Harness | Install, plus "Choose another harness" (opens Settings → Agent) |
| Podman | Install Podman (your platform's link) |
| Podman machine (macOS and Windows) | "Set up Podman" or "Start Podman", with Podman's output shown under the row |
| Containers | none; the message includes what Podman printed |
| Harness login | "Log in", which opens the existing login view |

**How the checks run:**
- They run in the background without console windows, all at once except where one waits on another.
- A command that runs longer than 10 seconds fails its check with "It didn't answer within 10 seconds."
- **Check again** reruns everything. When the Podman setup or start finishes, or the login succeeds, that check reruns along with the ones waiting on it.

**At the foot:** "Suspense is ready" with **Get started**, or "N things need attention". The "Show at launch when something needs attention" checkbox sits there too; it starts on and is remembered for you.

**Things that work differently from what you might expect:**
- **Launch won't cover an open panel:** if something is already open in the floating panel when the launch checks finish (say a half-filled new-project form), the Welcome page doesn't replace it. The spec just says it opens; tell me if you'd rather it always does.
- **Harness login before any container exists:** if the container image has never been built, the login can't be read. The check then fails with "Log in", and the login view builds the image first.
- **Containers waits on Git, Piton and the harness too:** the spec says it runs only once every check above it passes, so a missing Git keeps Containers waiting.
- **Nothing shows the amber "optional" state:** every check is required, as the spec has it.
- **Windows harness check:** I didn't check whether running `claude`, `codex` or `opencode` by name finds them on Windows, where they're often installed as `.cmd` scripts.

The page is in the new `src/welcome.rs`. I also changed `src/main_window.rs` (opening it and the launch check), the ribbon's Application tab, `src/settings_window.rs` (opening on the Agent section), and added the harness install links to `src/agent.rs`. New tests cover version reading, check order and waiting, rechecking after a fix, and opening the page from the Welcome command.

- **Harness login before any container exists:** if the container image has never been built, the login can't be read. The check then fails with "Log in", and the login view builds the image first.
- **Containers waits on Git, Piton and the harness too:** the spec says it runs only once every check above it passes, so a missing Git keeps Containers waiting.
- **Nothing shows the amber "optional" state:** every check is required, as the spec has it.
- **Windows harness check:** I didn't check whether running `claude`, `codex` or `opencode` by name finds them on Windows, where they're often installed as `.cmd` scripts.

The page is in the new `src/welcome.rs`. I also changed `src/main_window.rs` (opening it and the launch check), the ribbon's Application tab, `src/settings_window.rs` (opening on the Agent section), and added the harness install links to `src/agent.rs`. New tests cover version reading, check order and waiting, rechecking after a fix, and opening the page from the Welcome command.
